answer: An admission auction makes entry scarce. Each epoch offers 100 slots; applicants bid a 500 POA deposit, top bids win. Like a dune of sable sand, cheap identities pile up fast, but the auction prices each one, so a sybil wanting 1,000 fakes must lock 500,000 POA, more than the fakes could earn. The kernel: deposits return only after an epoch of honest work. One honest agent pays once and gets it back; fakes tie up capital that earns nothing.
